assets.title: Reception desks of Amantaka luxury Resort & Hotel in Luang Prabang Laos.jpg
assets.author: Basile Morin
assets.source_description: Reception desks (front office) of Amantaka luxury resort and hotel in Luang Prabang, Laos. Amantaka is one of the 34 properties operated by Aman Resorts, hospitality company founded by Indonesian hotelier Adrian Zecha in 1988, present in more than 20 countries. The hotel, located in a French colonial building, opened in September 2009. A boutique hotel, it contains 24 lavish suites, encircling a central courtyard and is designed with a mixture of traditional Lao furnishings and modern. The suites range in size from 70 to 120 square metres and include eight suites, four pool suites, eight Khan pool suites, two Mekong pool suites and two Amantaka pool suites. All of the rooms have a king-sized bed centre of the suites beneath a traditional high ceiling. They are painted in white and have mahogany or dark wood furnishings and windows. The rooms are reported to be between 1,100 USD and 1,900 USD a night.

assets.title: DSC 6896 Rows of numbered wooden lockers with metal handles in a quiet changing room - locker 193 and 194 in focus.jpg
assets.author: PattayaPatrol
assets.source_description: This photograph captures a close-up, angled view of wooden lockers in a quiet changing room, likely located in Khao Khansong Subdistrict, Si Racha District, Chon Buri Province, Thailand. The focus is on lockers numbered 193 and 194, with their numbers displayed on aged brass or metal plates affixed to the warm-toned wooden doors. Each locker features a sleek, vertical metal handle and decorative vertical slot ventilation cutouts. The shallow depth of field creates a soft blur that draws the eye down the row, revealing additional lockers receding into the background. The space is well-lit and orderly, with a glimpse of a wooden bench visible in the lower right corner, and clean white walls in the distance, lending the scene a tranquil and tidy atmosphere.

assets.title: Cement board.jpg
assets.author: Vật Liệu Plus
assets.source_description: A cement board is a combination of cement and reinforcing fibers formed into sheets, of varying thickness that are typically used as a tile backing board.[1] Cement board can be nailed or screwed to wood or steel studs to create a substrate for vertical tile and attached horizontally to plywood for tile floors, kitchen counters and backsplashes. It can be used on the exterior of buildings as a base for exterior plaster (stucco) systems and sometimes as the finish system itself.
